candidate_lesson.lesson_text: When the 30-indicator consensus shows high conviction (>90%) but green_matches=0 and hist_hr=0%, treat the signal as UNVALIDATED and freeze entries — high live conviction without any historical analog match is a novel unmemorized state, not an edge.
candidate_lesson.mechanism: green_matches counts how many times the current live indicator configuration has appeared in historical memory with a positive outcome. Zero matches means the ensemble has never seen this exact bull-alignment succeed before; conviction% only measures cross-sectional agreement of indicators right now, not the forward payoff of that agreement. Institutionally, a broad indicator stack lining up long with no historical precedent usually reflects a late-cycle crowded positioning snapshot rather than a repeatable inefficiency — the crowd is aligned, which is precisely when mean-reversion risk is highest.
candidate_lesson.testable_rule: if consensus_conviction > 0.90 and green_matches == 0 and hist_hr == 0.0: block_entry() # only trade conviction>0.90 when green_matches >= 3 (see GBPUSD hist_hr=68%, AUDUSD hist_hr=68%)
candidate_lesson.expected_impact: Filters out unvalidated high-conviction entries (EURUSD-type states); expected win-rate lift of +3-5% on consensus-driven trades and Sharpe contribution ~+0.02 by removing negative-expectancy novel states.
candidate_lesson.evidence_from_harvest: Live consensus shows EURUSD LONG at conv=92% but green_matches=0 / hist_hr=0%, versus GBPUSD LONG conv=100% green_matches=5 hist_hr=68% and AUDUSD LONG conv=100% green_matches=3 hist_hr=68%. The two pairs with historical matches carry a 68% memorized hit rate; the pair with identical directional conviction but zero matches has no validated edge — same conviction, opposite reliability.
